newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy repatriates 40 illegal Albanian immigrants.
newsitem.headline: Italy repatriates 40 illegal Albanian immigrants.

text.p: Italy said on Sunday it had repatriated 40 Albanian would-be illegal immigrants who had arrived in the southern town of Brindisi.
They met none of the conditions that would have allowed them to stay in Italy and were sent back to the port of Durres, near the capital Tirana, late on Saturday, regional officials said.
The would-be immigrants were a different group from the 70 Albanians who fled unrest in the southern port of Vlore and crossed the Adriatic on Friday.
Italy said on Saturday that the 70, some of whom had refused to board a boat which was earlier sent to repatriate them, could not stay in Italy unless they had proper papers.

"Although we understand their fear of being caught up in the disorder in the south...the government does not consider that the public order situation in the rest of the country presents conditions of emergency or other risks for personal safety," the foreign and interior ministries said in a joint statement.
The asylum-seekers were being put up by charitable groups while officials formally consider their cases individually. Those without legal entry papers will be sent back.

Tens of thousands of Albanians crossed to Italy in rusting freighters in 1991 after the collapse of 45 years of Stalinist rule in Europe's poorest state. Thousands more follow every year in illegal immigration rackets.
